newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel B surges 18.27 pct.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel B surges 18.27 pct.

text.p: Beer firm San Miguel Corp's B shares surged by 18.27 percent to 61.50 pesos in the first 30 minutes of trading on the Philippine Stock Exchange following the de facto devaluation of the peso.
The B shares are open to both foreign as well as local investors.
The company's A shares, available only to Filipinos, rose two pesos to 39.
Brokers said San Miguel's rise was part of the general surge in the market as a result of the sharp fall in the peso. Following the Central Bank's announcement, the peso fell just over 11 percent.
Manila stocks were battered in the past two days as the Central Bank raised overnight interest rates to a 2-1/2 year high of 32 percent.
The high rates were luring money away from equities to fixed income markets.
San Miguel was also seen benefiting from the peso's plunge as it has substantial operations abroad, brokers said. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841 8934
